name: Fidaxomicin
route_note: Oral tablets or granules for suspension twice daily for 10 days (extended-pulsed regimens also used).
targets: Bacterial RNA polymerase (switch region; rpoB/rpoC, sigma-dependent initiation)
owner: Merck & Co. (US); other licensees outside the US

discovery.by: Abbott Laboratories (tiacumicins); developed by Optimer Pharmaceuticals
discovery.note: A fermentation product of the actinomycete Dactylosporangium aurantiacum.

tagline: Narrow-spectrum gut-acting antibiotic for C. difficile with fewer recurrences
summary: Fidaxomicin is a narrow-spectrum macrocyclic antibiotic that acts within the gut against Clostridioides difficile while largely sparing the normal microbiota. Approved in 2011, it lowers recurrence compared with vancomycin and is preferred in several guidelines for initial and recurrent C. difficile infection.
mechanism: Fidaxomicin binds the 'switch region' of bacterial RNA polymerase at a site distinct from rifamycins, preventing the clamp from closing around promoter DNA and so blocking initiation of transcription. It is bactericidal against C. difficile and inhibits sporulation and toxin production.
Minimal systemic absorption and low activity against Bacteroides and other commensal anaerobes help preserve colonisation resistance, which is thought to underlie the lower recurrence rates.
uses: Clostridioides difficile infection in adults and children (initial episodes and recurrences)

history.title: Lipiarmycin
history.detail: Lepetit researchers describe lipiarmycin, later shown to be identical to tiacumicin B.

history.title: US and EU approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Dificid (May) and the EU authorises Dificlir (December) after two phase III trials showing fewer recurrences than vancomycin.

history.title: Merck acquisition
history.detail: Merck & Co. acquires Cubist, including Dificid.

history.title: Paediatric approval
history.detail: The FDA approves fidaxomicin for children aged 6 months and older.

history.title: Guideline preference
history.detail: IDSA/SHEA focused update recommends fidaxomicin over vancomycin for initial and recurrent C. difficile infection.

facts: Fidaxomicin is much more expensive than oral vancomycin, which has influenced its uptake despite guideline preference.
